concerns.text: T012 and T013 are marked [P] (parallel-safe) but explicitly depend on T011 (Download) completing first. The 'Sequential Logic' note correctly identifies this, but the [P] tag is semantically incorrect and misleading for parallel execution engines. T012 and T013 must be unmarked [P] or T011 must be split into a 'Download' task and a 'Verify' task if parallelism is intended after verification.

T018b and T018c are marked [P] but depend on T018a (Core FedAvg). T018b integrates DP into the core, and T018c orchestrates the loop calling T018b. These are strictly sequential. The [P] tags are invalid and violate the 'Producer before consumer' rule.

T024a, T024b, and T025 are marked [P] but depend on T035 (Filter utility collapse) and T027a (Filter time-limited). T035 depends on T027a. The 'Sequential Logic' note correctly states T027a and T035 must precede the stats tasks, yet the [P] tags on the stats tasks imply they can run in parallel with the filtering tasks or each other without dependency. This creates a race condition risk.
T028c is marked [P] but depends on T028a and T028b (aggregation and calculation). T028c generates the final summary CSV using data from T028a/b. These cannot run in parallel. The [P] tag is invalid.

T026 (Plotting) is marked [P] but depends on T025 (Sensitivity analysis results). The 'Sequential Logic' note correctly identifies this dependency, but the [P] tag contradicts it. T026 cannot run until T025 produces the data.

T011 is marked [P] but is a blocking prerequisite for T012 and T013. While it has no upstream dependencies, labeling it [P] in a list where downstream tasks are also [P] (incorrectly) creates confusion about the execution graph. It should be unmarked or the downstream tasks must be unmarked to reflect the true serial dependency chain.
